title: The terminal and the dashboard say the name too
description:
The MCP server is one of three surfaces that print a node id, and a name that only the plugin shows is a name that makes the three disagree.

The terminal: packages/cli/src/queue.ts:22 and packages/cli/src/distribute.ts:70 both join bare ids into a sentence, packages/cli/src/hook.ts:158 prints `<id> (waiting on …)` in the message that denies a spawn — which is the one a person reads while being stopped, and therefore the one that most needs to say what was stopped — and packages/cli/src/sync.ts:25 lists ids through `named()`. Check `status.ts` and `board.ts` for the same shape before assuming that list is complete.

The dashboard: check what the canvas and the panel show today before changing anything. If a node already renders its title on the canvas, the name may belong only where space is short — a label under a circle, a chip in a list — and not everywhere at once. Read apps/dashboard/src/canvas/paint.ts and apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx first and say in the brief what you found; do not add a second label beside a title that is already legible.

Use the same form the MCP surface uses. Two vocabularies for one board is the thing packages/cli/src/work.ts and apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts already argue against for the log marks, and it is the same argument here.
